title: Peril of Cymbaline Isle - Interlude
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w3HciqK70s4

Daniel (@dungeondive) pauses the campaign for an honest check-in, and the most interesting admission is about the filming rather than the game. Playing a solo RPG on camera makes him feel he is scripting entertainment rather than discussing a board game — more emotionally draining, more pressure to stay on top of a story he is inventing as he goes. He plans to wrap the cult thread and shift to self-contained adventures with recurring characters, imagining it as *Cheers*: the regulars at the Crooked Violin, named by Dungeon Dive patrons, are the thing he has enjoyed most.

The tool audit is useful for anyone assembling their own kit. *Scarlet Heroes* he now rates as possibly his favourite RPG system — the right balance of light rules and a little crunch, with hopping vampires as a bonus. Table Fables earns its ubiquity. The Folklore rumour cards he calls one of the best expansion decks ever made. His card-based overland travel system, measured in days rather than distance, he is keeping.

What failed is instructive too: Warhammer Quest and Dungeon Universalis event decks proved too welded to their own games, and the *Tome of Adventure Design* is too vast to use on the fly. Too many tables, he notes, and you need a table of tables.

----

Which random-generation books actually get used at your table, and which turned out to be too big to open mid-session?
